import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_65/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_65/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Perform join on ['fname', 'day'] as specified
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, how='inner', left_on=['fname', 'day'], right_on=['fname', 'day'])

# Group by Source2_65_0.fname and count occurrences of fname in Source2_65_0 (which is df0)
# Since after join, rows correspond to matched rows, counting df0.fname occurrences in joined is counting rows per fname
# But the operation history says group by Source2_65_0.fname, count(Source2_65_0.fname) as row_count
# So group by df0.fname in the joined dataframe and count rows

# The joined dataframe has 'fname' column from both sides merged, so just group by 'fname' and count rows
result = df_joined.groupby('fname', as_index=False).size().rename(columns={'size': 'row_count'})

# Ensure the schema matches target: ['fname': string, 'row_count': integer]
result['fname'] = result['fname'].astype(str)
result['row_count'] = result['row_count'].astype(int)

# Write to target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_65/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_65/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename columns in source0 to match join keys exactly if needed
# source0 columns: ['ï»¿index', 'cop', 'day', 'fname', 'by', 'Ok?', 'remarks']
# source1 columns: ['Slice n°', 'X', 'Y', 'Distance', 'Pixel Value', 'ok_col_names', 'ok_col_num', 'ok_row_num', 'cop_name', 'day', 'fname']

# Join on 'fname' and 'day' columns (both present in both tables)
